observation: The compact numeral is heavily retraced. A long curved upper entry and lower loop favor 6, while an extra upright at its left could be a separate 1 or part of the retracing. No independent cancellation stroke is secure enough to assign a deleted state.

Thm is abbreviated and underlined, without a secure full stop. The beginning of Considérons is crossed by sloping marginal writing; the later di/é/rons-like bodies and les are clearer, so the word remains locally uncertain. The diagonal strokes above and below the baseline are excluded as marginal-note spillover rather than treated as cancellation of this heading.

Deux is raised above the line and attached before catégories by a long bent leader, not an underline. Catégories has separate upper marks over é and i. Two word groups after it are crossed at body height; ci-après and définies remain tentative because the strike merges their lower letters and the latter's tall stems. The two points of the final colon are separate and not cancelled.

The list label before celle is partly mixed with diagonal margin ink and remains tentative. The old word has a long p descender, a tall l and an -es ending; its covered first bodies favor couples over triples. Systèmes is raised above as the replacement, with a separate upper accent-like mark. The long vertical stroke at the old word's left also receives the descender of the raised word, so it is not treated as decisive evidence for an old t.

The first X has a separate bent upper tilde and a small star at the upper right. The second X is drawn over a cap-and-stem form resembling T; whether that older form is a deliberate cancellation remains uncertain. A distinct dot lies above it, and a separate dense raised blob lies to its right. The latter has no recoverable internal strokes, so the superscript empty unsure records present unreadable ink. E has the open double-curved calligraphic form. The high curved stroke between the first two objects descends from the prose above and is excluded.
Espace is written out; top. is abbreviated with a distinct point, followed by a separate large comma. The tiny upper-edge hooked stroke belongs to the preceding line and is excluded.

Both words are written in full. Cylindrique has a long descending y, looped l, separate i dots and long q descender. The isolated ascenders and formula marks entering from below are neighboring-line context.

Esp. has a visible abbreviation point. After top the visible mark is a comma, with no separate preceding point. The X has an independent dot and the connector to Y is a plain horizontal shaft without a visible head. Application and continue are written out. The final punctuation has a separate upper point and lower comma stroke, read as a semicolon.

Cônique has an independent shallow circumflex over its o. The two word groups after the full stop are crossed through their lower bodies; the first is obscured and remains tentative, while the second has the tall A and l followed by ors. The raised ci-dessus entering at the lower edge belongs to the following line and is excluded from this target.

The short first word is crossed by a separate horizontal stroke. Alors is live here. Foncteur begins with a long descending f; naturel and de are on the baseline. Ci-dessus is raised and attaches between naturel and de with a bent returning leader; the curl at its right is continuous with that leader, not a secure comma.

The upright target is the slanting marginal note, beginning NB; the main heading and body words now descend diagonally across it and are excluded. Une variante and the short wording before en termes de are difficult where the hands cross, so they remain tentative without a grammatical completion. Voisinages tubulaires, stricts, au lieu de germes, de voisinages tub., catégories, équivalentes and pour simplifier are the clearest stretches. Stricts has a separate underline. The compact black group between sont and équivalentes has no recoverable prose letters and uncertain cancellation state. At the lower left the narrow upright followed by a 2-like curve is retained as i-subscript-2 versus 12; its preceding attachment and the final closing parenthesis cannot be made into a complete construction from this ink.

The tilde is a detached wavy stroke. The raised mark at its X's right is densely retraced; an oblique upper ray and several short crossing strokes suggest a star, retained with doubt. The amalgamation sign has two upright arms joined to a flat lower bar. Its lower X carries a separate round point high at the right; there is no final punctuation in the target.

Only the upper-left marginal NB note is transcribed; the second NB, large X and long curved attachment at the lower right are body-text spillover. The formula has a separate tilde and star on its first X, and an independent point on its second X. A small cross-like mark sits below the left opening parenthesis and is retained locally without assigning it a mathematical role. Découpe has a separate acute and cônique a shallow independent arch. The final calligraphic character after Y is retraced where its roof and lower loop meet the closing parenthesis, hence the local doubt. No terminal full stop is secure.

NB has a distinct underline. The initial capital of Une is heavily retraced and crossed near its roof by a long bent attachment line; an independent cancellation through the whole word is not secure, so its state remains doubtful. X-prime is raised after partie and before de. The mark after donc consists of a small upper stroke and a compact lower body, favoring à but also resembling two colon points. The long line entering from above is an attachment, not an opening parenthesis or an underline.

The first X has a separate tilde, prime and heavily inked star; the X after de has a star but no visible tilde in this frame. The two Y forms differ by a prime. Ayant has a long descending y and final rising t. The trailing relation has a straight upper stroke and a curved lower stroke; no separate third bar is secure, so inclusion is preferred with local doubt about an added equality bar.

Inverse begins with a distinct dotted i and continues through a low n/v run to the final se-like strokes. The X after dans has a separate upper point. Fermé has a tall f whose descender continues below the frame, and a separate acute over its ending; there is no additional full written word between fermé and the compact ssi at the right edge. Neighboring lower-line letters are excluded.

A continuous horizontal strike crosses the lower Pour que X-prime soit, including the X and final tall t. The same wording is rewritten above it, with its own prime and no crossing strike. The curved stroke entering at the upper right is the descender from the previous line, excluded from this revision.

Two long horizontal strikes cross the old wording: the lower passes through il f. et, the obscured short s-like group, que and X-prime; the upper crosses the raised une description. The letter group et is retraced and the short following group is partly buried in the lower strike. A dense star-like mark lies at the old X's lower right; its level is closer to a subscript, but association with an upper star remains uncertain. The replacement below reads il f et s. que l'on ait, with no visible point after its f and a distinct point after s. The old f does have a separate point. The raised phrase's exact attachment within the discarded wording is uncertain.

The left E is a rounded calligraphic form with upper and lower lobes. In the parenthesized pair the first X has only a wavy tilde, with no visible star or prime; the second has a separate centered point. The curled fragment entering at the upper right is excluded as neighboring context.

Lieu has a looped l followed by the dotted i and low eu; the tall straight stroke above its end descends from the preceding line and is not a final t. Remplacer has a clear descending p and ascending l. The displayed X has a separate tilde and prime, with no star. Neighboring formula tops entering from below are excluded.

The raised left group has a detached tilde, thick prime and separate lower 1. Below and to its right is X-prime intersection X-epsilon, covered by a long horizontal overbar; its right endpoint is thickened but has no distinct two-sided arrowhead. No equals sign is visible between the raised group and the lower expression, so none is supplied. The superscript on the right X has the two-lobed epsilon form rather than clear star rays. Clipped neighboring writing at the top and bottom left is excluded.

At the left edge a curved entry and very compressed dotted abbreviation are visible; i.e. is preferred, with uncertainty about whether the curve also supplies an opening parenthesis. The equation has a star on the first X, a wavy tilde on the next and a separate dot on the final X, separated by a single descending oblique set-minus stroke. A closing parenthesis and comma follow. Germe is fully written with a long g descender. The last X has tilde, prime and lower 1. The compressed ending has an a/u-like point-and-low-stroke group, then v/o, a dotted i, s and a final point, retained as au vois. with local doubt and without expansion.
Two lighter, thinner digits each have a curved upper entry, descending diagonal and long lower foot, read as 22. The black strip below is the page edge, not a cancellation.
